body.p: There was a period of my life when I was living off an inheritance. I took on small freelance obligations, but my days were mostly free. On the weekends, I was taking the bus to Providence, at the start of a new relationship. During the week, I was prancing around Lower Manhattan, flirting with retail workers and trying on clothes.

One day, I was sitting with a coffee on Lafayette, when I saw this chic woman walking up from Houston. She had purpose in her step, underscored by her outfit: a slender floral dress with a complementary color head wrap.
As she came closer, I realized I recognized her.
“Miche?”

I went to college with Miche, but she really only makes sense to me now that TikTok exists. First of all, she's beautiful. Second of all, she talks like a TED Talk or a conspiracy theorist — a tremble in the voice that might be the situational urgency, or maybe it’s just the surfacing of some part of the self that is actually listening to what the hell this body is saying.
She is the type who finds comfort and ease directly addressing a forward facing camera and Instagram Live.

Recently I tap scanned her 38-part story. Every thirty minutes or so, for hours, she posts. 13 hours ago, she gets ready for bed. 12 hours ago, she's pajamas. She tucks herself in. 10 hours ago, wide eyed, she's screaming laughter into the camera from her pillow. 9 hours ago she turns out her light. 8 hours ago, memes and more dramatic zooms, reactions and screaming. 6 hours ago, the sun rises. Then she's on the street...
I stopped. She never went to sleep. She just started the next day.
She looked at me like a sleepwalker confronted in the living room, and then she smiled. “Oh my god, hi!”
“Wow! I'm so happy to see it's you,” I said. “I saw you walking from Houston and I was thinking, ‘She has great style.’ What are you doing over here?”
“Ugh, I'm having such a crazy day, I've just been all over the place, I've been to like six stores — and the only reason I got out of meetings was to say I was going for lunch.”
“Ooh, she's frequently invited. Where are you working these days?”
“Yeah, well I just have all these projects I'm supposed to oversee. I'm the CEO of LeapFrog.”
“You're the CEO of LeapFrog?”
“Yeah, yeah. Their offices are right there,” she said pointing towards Great Jones Street. We both looked and let the beat skip.
“Anyway, do you know where I can buy a bathing suit?”
She shook her face as if a fly had landed on it. “You know what, never mind, I really gotta go. You think H&M is open?”
“It's like 2 PM”
“You're right, I should get back. Ok talk to you later!” And off she went.
